data.narrative:
BlackSea Technologies is a platform-stage company in the Defense & Security sector. The comparable universe consists of 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers, including Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems.

The peer-median method is not applicable in this case. A review of 22 same-sector peers identified zero companies at the same stage, zero at adjacent stages, and zero in a similar valuation tier. The narrow filtering required to establish a meaningful peer set—essential for platform-stage valuations where stage and scale divergence creates wide valuation spreads—yielded insufficient datapoints (need ≥3). Relying on an all-sector median would introduce substantial noise given the heterogeneity of Defense & Security subsectors and business models.

Without a sufficient narrow peer cohort, standard triangulation cannot be performed. Valuation support would require alternative methods: precedent transactions within Defense & Security platform exits, discounted cash flow analysis anchored to disclosed metrics, or qualitative assessment against the named private peer set. Each approach carries distinct limitations. Until additional data on comparable platform-stage exits or target-specific financials are available, a quantitative valuation range cannot be responsibly derived. The key uncertainty is the absence of sufficient near-peer trading or exit data to establish reliable multiples or discount rates specific to this stage and sector.
